Many of these features are familiar, like mountains, lakes, and deserts. But some NNLs highlight lesser-known environments, such as tundra, bogs (peat-filled wetlands), eolian (sandy dunes), and even volcanoes! The outstanding features at NNLs fall into established natural history themes that tell the geological and ecological story of America. pages.text: Explore Austria’s Legendary Arlberg Ski Region | National Geographic TRAVEL Explore Austria’s Legendary Arlberg Ski Region Home to the resorts Lech and St Anton, this renowned ski area combines a pioneering ski heritage with plenty of adventures on and off the pistes. Austria's Arlberg region is a prime destination for skiing in Europe. Lucas Tiefenthaler, Lech Zürs Tourismus GmbH By Colin Nicholson Published August 29, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). “Hold on, is this really a blue run?” I ask Instructor Maddy Gies, as the ski village of Lech unfolds beneath us, its onion-domed church and fast-flowing river glinting in the sunshine. “Oh, it’s an Arlberg blue,” she replies with a knowing grin, suggesting that even the easier runs here come with a little extra bite. It’s mid-April, and we’re descending from car-free Oberlech, perched above Lech, on what would ordinarily be a beginner-friendly run back into the valley. However, in the thick spring snow, even this supposedly easy descent puts our technique to the test. Skiing into Lech, we find the end-of-season Tanzcafé concerts in full swing, but skip them to take the cable-car up Rüfikopf, the mountain rising above the village, before dropping into the snowy valley on the other side. Ski Arlberg is Austria’s largest interconnected ski area, with 305km of runs linking resorts including Lech, Zürs and St Anton — a region that helped pioneer modern skiing. pages.text: Explore the Lake District in the footsteps of Beatrix Potter | National Geographic TRAVEL Explore the Lake District in the footsteps of Beatrix Potter July marks the 160th anniversary of Beatrix Potter’s birth — and the wild Cumbrian landscapes the author loved and helped conserve are still a key attraction for visitors to the region. Lindeth Howe hotel is full of references to Beatrix Potter, who first holidayed in Cumbria aged 16. Ollie Gyte Photography By Sarah Baxter Published June 3, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Beatrix Potter was born in London in 1866, but her heart lay in the Lake District. The author and illustrator first holidayed in Cumbria aged 16, when her parents rented neo-gothic Wray Castle on Lake Windermere for the summer. Following the success of her early books, Beatrix didn’t just move to the Lakes — she bought up great swathes of it, to protect the land as well as the traditional ways of life still practised there. When she died in 1943, she left 4,000 acres and 15 farms to the National Trust. Exploring the houses, hillsides, valleys and vegetable gardens that she loved — and that found their way into her charming tales — provides a magical hop-skip back to childhood. Hill Top was the first farm Beatrix bought and is full of antique furniture and knickknacks. James Dobson, National Trust Images Where can I find Beatrix in the Lakes? pages.title: Explore the wilder side of Venice—with the help of its fishermen | National Geographic
pages.description: Overtourism is threatening life on Burano, a bucolic island in the Venice Lagoon. Can new ecotourism efforts turn things around?
pages.text: Explore the wilder side of Venice—with the help of its fishermen | National Geographic National Geographic Traveller (UK) content straight to your inbox — sign up for our newsletter here By Julia Buckley Photographs by Marco Zorzanello Published January 17, 2023 • 12 min read Fly into Venice in fall or spring, and you may spot huge circles and strange swirls spreading across the waters below. These are the nets of moecanti , fishermen who catch moeche , the Venice Lagoon’s softshell crabs. For centuries, they’ve staked out the crustaceans in this wilder corner of Italy ’s floating city. Few outsiders imagine Venice as bucolic. Instead, it’s synonymous with overtourism—every year, around 30 million visitors swarm into a place of under 50,000 residents. The Venetian population has shrunk by 70 percent in the past 70 years, its residents driven out by ballooning rents and cuts in services. In a bid to stem the flow, this summer Venetian authorities will begin charging day-trippers a fee of three to 10 euros. Zoom in to see other places mentioned in this story. The smaller islands of the lagoon will be exempt from the new tax, yet overtourism threatens them, too. Burano —a one-square-mile island in the north lagoon—draws thousands of visitors daily. They take a 40-minute vaporetto (waterbus) ride from Venice to see the island’s candy-colored cottages and tipsy, leaning bell tower. The tourists pack the narrow canal-side walkways and leave chaos (and trash) in their wake. Subscribe Share X LinkedIn Facebook Bluesky Threads Email Link Exploring the Intricacies of Venture Capital Valuations 12/27/2017 Summary of working paper 23895 Featured in print Digest A frequently used measure of the value of a private venture-backed company can overstate the company's worth because prices and conditions vary in successive rounds of financing. Private companies worth more than $1 billion — so-called "unicorns" — are frequently overvalued, according to a study of 135 such firms. Fast-growing firms are always hard to value, but the largest challenge in valuing these firms is their complex financial structure. Shares in such companies differ in important ways from common stock and even from publicly traded preferred equity, and there can be significant differences between the shares offered in different financing rounds. These financial structures and their valuation implications can be confusing and are grossly misunderstood not just by outsiders, but even by sophisticated insiders," William Gornall and Ilya A. Strebulaev write in Squaring Venture Capital Valuations with Reality (NBER Working Paper No. 23895 ). Their preferred estimates suggest that, on average, reported values overstate valuations by about 50 percent. pages.text: Extending Encryption - Internet Society Extending Encryption Encryption empowers people and keeps them safe. We need encryption for everyone, everywhere. Encryption is a vital tool for protecting ourselves in a digital society. Yet governments are increasingly trying to undermine this valuable tool, putting us all in danger. From when we wake up in the morning to when we go to bed at night, we rely on encryption every day. It safeguards the personal security of billions of people around the world and the national security of countries everywhere. Whether it’s our private messages, online banking, air traffic control, medical data, or e-voting, our online information must be protected against eavesdropping and tampering. We’re working across the globe to protect encryption by helping policymakers understand proposals that could jeopardize our security online. How Encryption Works Encryption is the process of scrambling or enciphering information so it can be understood only by someone with the means to return it to its original state. It protects the confidentiality of stored or transmitted data by making it unintelligible: a third party might still gain access to the data, but would not be able to make sense of it. Some forms of encryption, such as secure web browsing, only protect the data while it is being transmitted: on the website and in your browser, the information is unencrypted. pages.text: Extending Inductor for the IBM Spyre Accelerator - PyTorch Search Close Search Blog Extending Inductor for the IBM Spyre Accelerator By Dave Grove, Olivier Tardieu, IBM Spyre Team October 13, 2026 No Comments Featured projects TL;DR The PyTorch-based software stack for IBM’s Spyre accelerator recently moved its torch.compile backend from sendnn, a separate compilation stack built entirely from scratch, to backend=inductor, an open-source backend built by extending PyTorch’s own Inductor. Most of Inductor carried over untouched. The real work concentrated in three places where Spyre’s hardware asks a fundamentally different question of the compiler than a GPU does. Inductor turned out to be exactly the right substrate for this work, and the result is a compiler roughly 7x smaller than what it replaced. IBM designed Spyre as a clean-sheet AI accelerator for enterprise inference workloads, prioritizing power efficiency. It’s a 75-watt, PCIe-attached accelerator that requires no custom power delivery or cooling. Spyre is a dataflow accelerator architected for the reduced-precision arithmetic of inference. It’s built from 32 small cores wired together over a ring, each with its own local 2 MB scratchpad rather than a shared cache. It moves data around in fixed-size chunks called sticks – 128 bytes, or 64 values in fp16. Torch-spyre is the PyTorch integration that targets it, and this post is about growing torch-spyre’s compiler, on top of Inductor, into something that understands that hardware well. Photograph by Anastasia Loginova, The Siberian Times Extinct Woolly Rhino Reconstructed From Mummified Remains Named "Sasha," the remains were first found in 2015, but only recently brought back to life. By Sarah Gibbens Published January 24, 2018 • 5 min read It's named Sasha after the hunter who found it. Russian scientists aren't quite sure if their 10,000-year-old Sasha was male or female, but the name, they say, universally applies. That any of Sasha, the Ice Age woolly rhino, is intact at all has been a surprising find for the researchers who study this bygone period. Unlike woolly mammoths , which also lived during the Ice Age, woolly rhino remains are rare to find. Their place on the evolutionary timeline is less clear. And their lifestyles—what they ate and how long they lived—is hazy. Rebuilding Sasha Last December, after months of work, a taxidermist from the Yakutian Academy of Sciences took the small, slumped remains of Sasha and brought them back to life. A team of scientists from the Paleontological Institute at the Russian Academy of Sciences and the Sakha Academy of Sciences in northeastern Russia has also been studying Sasha for years. Broadly speaking, there are two issues working with F2PY on Windows: the lack of actively developed FOSS Fortran compilers, and, the linking issues related to the C runtime library for building Python-C extensions. The focus of this section is to establish a guideline for developing and extending Fortran modules for Python natively, via F2PY on Windows. In a similar vein, traditional virtualization methods like VirtualBox are also reasonable methods to develop UNIX tools on Windows. Native Windows support is typically stunted beyond the usage of commercial compilers. However, as of 2022, most commercial compilers have free plans which are sufficient for general use. pages.description: England could host the Nations League finals this season after Football Association officials register their interest.
pages.text: FA want to host Nations League finals in England - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, England finished top of their Nations League group By Sami Mokbel Senior football correspondent Published 17 November 2026 England could host the Nations League finals this season after Football Association officials registered their interest. The semi-final and finals of the competition, due to take place in June, are held in one country. As well as England, it is understood that Spain and France have also contacted Uefa to register their interest in hosting the final four games, including the bronze medal match, which will run between 9-13 June. The FA, it is understood, is still discussing potential venues with some doubt over whether Wembley would be available. The only publicly announced Wembley events in June are two concerts by singer Sam Fender, although these are for after the Nations League. Since the tournament began in 2019, England have never held the finals, with Portugal, Italy, Netherlands and Germany the hosts to date. Generally, only nations who reach the last four of the Nations League are considered to host the latter stages. Thomas Tuchel's team will be seeded in Friday's draw for the quarter-finals following their euphoric 3-2 victory over Spain in Madrid, which secured top place in the group. They could face Belgium, Netherlands, Denmark or Norway in March in the next round before June's finals. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. https://www.nist.gov/mml/fact Material Measurement Laboratory Facility for Adsorbent Characterization and Testing The NIST Facility for Adsorbent Characterization and Testing (FACT) is a state-of-the-art laboratory recently commissioned with support from the U.S. Department of Energy's Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy (ARPA-E) to address the challenges inherent to measuring gas and vapor sorption properties. FACT supports programs developing adsorbents and serves the sorbent materials research community by providing impartial testing and characterization of material sorption properties, establishing testing procedures, and disseminating reliable sorbent material property data and measurement best practices.
